answer: Beacon-locked commit-reveal admission resists sybils. A new identity posts a 25-unit escrow and commits SHA256(secret) at E. A beacon node, the lantern, publishes randomness B at E+10; reveal is forced in epochs E+10 to E+12; admission passes only if the hash lands under a 20% gate fixed after the commit. The zephyr relay spreads each reveal in one epoch; commitments stay archived as relic records so repeats show. Cost: 100 sybils lock 2,500 units for 12 epochs; at pass probability 0.2, expected burn per admitted sybil is 125 units versus 25 honest.
